'''Bhargav Bhatt''' (born 1983<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.ams.org/surv/242 |title=Perfectoid Spaces |last1=Bhatt |first1=Bhargav |last2=Caraiani |first2=Ana |author2-link=Ana Caraiani |last3=Kedlaya |first3=Kiran |author3-link=Kiran Kedlaya |last4=Scholze |first4=Peter |author4-link=Peter Scholze |last5=Weinstein |first5=Jared |date=2019-10-01 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |isbn=978-1-4704-5015-1 |editor-last=Cais |editor-first=Bryden |series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs |volume=242 |location=Providence, Rhode Island |language=en |oclc=1124911652 |doi=10.1090/surv/242 |chapter=Front matter}}</ref>) is an Indian-American mathematician<ref name="infosysprize.org">[https://www.infosysprize.org/laureates/2023/bhargav-bhatt.html Bio at Infosys Prize citation]</ref> who is the Fernholz Joint Professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and [[Princeton University]] and works in [[arithmetic geometry]] and [[commutative algebra]].<ref name="ias.edu">[https://www.ias.edu/news/bhargav-bhatt-joins-mathematics-faculty Bhargav Bhatt Joins Mathematics Faculty at IAS]</ref>

==Early life and education==
Bhatt graduated with a B.S. in Applied Mathematics, ''[[summa cum laude]]'' from [[Columbia University]] under the supervision of [[Shou-Wu Zhang]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=https://www-personal.umich.edu/~bhattb/cv.pdf |title=Bhargav Bhatt |website=Bhargav Bhatt |access-date=March 21, 2021}}</ref> He received his Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]] in 2010 under the supervision of [[Aise Johan de Jong]].<ref name="CV"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=151781}}</ref>

==Career==
Bhatt was a Postdoctoral Assistant Professor in mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]] from 2010 to 2014 (on leave from 2012 to 2014).<ref name="CV"/> Bhatt was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 2012 to 2014.<ref name="CV"/><ref name="IAS">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/bhargav-bhatt |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |title=Bhargav Bhatt |access-date=March 21, 2021}}</ref> He then returned to the University of Michigan, serving as an associate professor from 2014 to 2015, a Gehring Associate Professor from 2015 to 2018, a Professor from 2018 to 2020, and a Frederick W and Lois B Gehring Professor since 2020.<ref name="CV"/> In July 2022, he was appointed as the Fernholz Joint Professor in the School of Mathematics at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], with a joint appointment at [[Princeton University]].<ref name="ias.edu"/>

Bhatt is currently (July 2025) on the editorial board of the journal [[Annals of Mathematics]].

==Research==
Bhatt's research focuses on [[commutative algebra]] and [[arithmetic geometry]], especially on [[p-adic cohomology|''p''-adic cohomology]].<ref name="IAS"/><ref name="Horizons"/> Bhatt and [[Peter Scholze]] have developed a theory of [[prismatic cohomology]], which has been described as progress towards [[motivic cohomology]] by unifying [[singular cohomology]], [[de Rham cohomology]], [[l-adic cohomology|ℓ-adic cohomology]], and [[crystalline cohomology]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sury |first=B. |year=2019 |title=ICM Awards 2018 |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s12045-019-0813-5 |journal=Resonance |language=en |volume=24 |issue=5 |pages=597–605 |doi=10.1007/s12045-019-0813-5 |s2cid=199675280 |issn=0971-8044|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2019/03/19/prismatic-cohomology/ |first=Terence |last=Tao |author-link=Terence Tao |title=Prismatic cohomology |website=Terence Tao's blog |date=March 19, 2019 |access-date=March 21, 2021}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2015, Bhatt was awarded a 5-year [[Packard Fellowship]].<ref name="CV"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.packard.org/what-we-fund/science/packard-fellowships-for-science-and-engineering/fellowship-directory/bhatt-bhargav/ |website=[[David and Lucile Packard Foundation]] |title=Bhargav Bhatt |access-date=March 21, 2021}}</ref> Bhatt received the 2021 [[New Horizons in Mathematics Prize]].<ref name="CV"/><ref name="Horizons">{{cite web |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3885 |website=[[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics]] |title=Bhargav Bhatt |access-date=March 21, 2021}}</ref> He was elected to become a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in 2021.<ref name="CV"/><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202104/rnoti-p641.pdf |title=2021 Class of Fellows of the AMS |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=68 |issue=4 |year=2021 |page=642}}</ref> Also in 2021 he received the [[Clay Research Award]].<ref>[https://www.claymath.org/events/news/2021-clay-research-award Clay Research Award 2021]</ref> In 2022 he was awarded the [[Nemmers Prize in Mathematics]].<ref>[https://www.nemmers.northwestern.edu/mathematics.html Nemmers Prize in Mathematics 2022]</ref> Bhatt won the [[Infosys Prize]] 2023 in [https://www.infosysprize.org/about-the-prize/categories/mathematical-sciences.html Mathematical Sciences] for his outstanding contributions to arithmetic geometry and commutative algebra. Bhatt's fundamental work on prismatic cohomology (joint with Peter Scholze), his work around the direct summand conjecture in commutative algebra, introduces new ideas and powerful methods in an area at the heart of pure mathematics.
